title: Innocent Bystanders
subtitle: Deny involvement all you like, you're still in the thick of it.

content.text: A masquerade ball is taking place in Montmartre. It lacks a clear theme, but a mask is required for entry. So you pick up:
A polished silver mask with a polite smile
A rough wooden mask carved with totem motifs
An enamel mask adorned with multicolored feathers
A lifelike paper mask painted to match your face

branch.text: Pretend, for now, that you are still yourself.

content.text: A masquerade ball is taking place in Montmartre. It lacks a clear theme, but a mask is required for entry. So you pick up:
A polished silver mask with a polite smile
A rough wooden mask carved with totem motifs
An enamel mask adorned with multicolored feathers
A lifelike paper mask painted to match your face

branch.text: Pretend, for now, that you are still yourself.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Please, follow the officer outside and leave your contact details before you go.
The shocked crowd file out like penned sheep, bleating and chattering with each step.

items.speaker: Participant I
items.text: I doubt I'll get any sleep tonight after that sight.

items.speaker: Participant II
items.text: I told you we shouldn't have come! Nothing good ever comes of fortune-telling!

items.speaker: Participant III
items.text: What could explain all that? Hysteria? A disease, perhaps?

items.speaker: Participant I
items.text: It's possible. You know, Fabio and Franco told me their neighbor started ranting about fighting alongside Cardinal Richelieu. Next thing you know, the man's leapt out the window riding a broom. Still in the hospital, I hear.

items.speaker: Participant II
items.text: But remember what she said earlier? Maybe what she saw was her own killer.

items.speaker: Participant I
items.text: You mean the Beasts of Gévaudan?
Fear, and a trace of hidden excitement, creeps onto every guest's face. The century-old legend casts its terrifying shadow once again.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Ladies and gentlemen!

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: We will begin our investigation immediately. In the meantime, we ask that you not spread any rumors. There's no cause for panic as of now.
The murmurs fade but the officer's words have done little to calm them.
The crowd disperses, leaving behind a few key witnesses.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: This isn't going to get pinned on me, is it? I didn't even touch her! You'll testify for me, won't you, Félicienne?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Félicienne?
Adèle turns back to find her employer pacing around the corpse, eyes gleaming with curiosity.

items.speaker: Félicienne
items.text: Our so-called prophet failed to see her own demise. Well, if this isn't an interesting twist ...

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: What are you doing? Get over here before they scold you for disturbing a crime scene!
She sighs inwardly at her employer's whims, relieved the nearby officer isn't paying attention.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Ah, not these Beasts of Gévaudan again.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Again? What do you mean, Benjamin?
She's fortunate to have found a familiar face among the arriving officers.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: *sigh* It's just a rumor and a wild one at that. Yet somehow, it's spread to every corner of Paris!

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: There have been a number of sightings of these so-called "beasts," but by the time we arrive at the scene, there isn't so much as a trace left of them—not even a hair!

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: The whole world's gone mad. Street crime is on the rise, and the last case we asked you for help with identification on? Well, that was completely ... *sigh*
He presses his hand to his temple, giving it a soft rub.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: As if we don't have enough to deal with! Half the city's on strike, and every day there's some new trouble, whether from the factories or out on the streets!

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: I envy you, Adèle. How simple it must be to sit behind a wheel all day and show visitors around.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Oh, well, it comes with its own set of problems.
Adèle glances toward Félicienne. She seems to have lost interest in the corpse and is now intent on examining a chair in the corner.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Heh. Knew you'd say that.
The officer pulls out a notebook and pen. When he looks up again, he adopts his best attempt at a professional tone.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Let's get on with it. There are some questions we need you to answer. You know how these things go.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: I trust you know this is strictly procedure. You were the person closest to the victim at the time of death. So please, Adèle, answer with care.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Go ahead. Ask away, officer.
The evidence has been cleared away. The coroner examines the body with visible concern. The diviner's death is gruesome indeed.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Blue lips, dilated pupils, clenched fists, and a stiffened spine ... The coroner will have his say, I'm sure, but it looks like extreme shock to me.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Extreme shock? But ...

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: What were the circumstances of the event? Anything unusual?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: The madame offered to read my fate, but halfway through, she started acting strange, staring at me and mumbling things.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: She said something about a beast and then collapsed to the floor.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: So, she was reading your fortune, saw a Beast of Gévaudan, and it what? Scared her to death?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: It sounds ridiculous, I know, Benjamin, but it's what I saw.
They exchange a glance.
The officer's pen hesitates, weighing how much of the madness is worth writing down.
Finally, he closes the notebook with a resigned look.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Okay. Thanks for your help, Adèle. I suppose it's about time we tied all these cases concerning the beasts together.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: But it's strange, no? How could creatures from a folktale more than a century old be doing all this here and now?

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: This has to be more than a passing fad. Paris—hell, the entire country—has been gripped by all sorts of rumors. The streets are growing more volatile by the day.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: You're right. There are always people who will try to take advantage of these situations.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Like this poor fortune-teller. I bet she heard some tales about my family and thought she could scam me with a sensational prophecy about my not-so-rosy fate.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: "Doomed to die on a quest for hidden jewels." Seems the madame didn't know that you're the furthest thing from a treasure hunter.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: It's hardly a secret that the Taverniers have a habit of meeting an unfortunate end.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Far from it. Which is why I didn't believe her for a moment. The Tavernier Curse? Please, it's just a story made up to dramatize the legends of my ancestors.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: From my great-great-great-great-great-great-grandfather, who died after bringing the French Blue from India,

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: down to my great-grandfather, who died chasing jewelry stolen from France during the Revolution.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Call it a curse, if you like—a mystical power, fate, coincidence—whatever the words, the plain and dull truth is that hunting jewels is a dangerous line of work, no?

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: That it is. While we're on the topic, how are your parents doing? I recall you said they were still in the family business.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Out on some quest again. I couldn't even hazard a guess as to where they are now; they move around so often.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: But they have sent letters. Living life to the fullest, as far as I can tell.
The officer exhales in relief.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: *relieved sigh* Glad to hear it. Maybe I should envy them instead. Traveling the world like that ... Much better than being stuck in a police station.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: And you? Don't you ever think of joining them on the hunt?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: My parents and I are different, to say the least. I don't share their obsession with shiny stones.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: A simple, comfortable life—that's all I want. No glittering ambitions, no fancy things, just a job that pays the bills, fills my belly, and lets me get a good night's sleep at the end of the day. Why anyone would want to think so hard every day is beyond me.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: In fact, this job was the first thing I saw when I opened the advertisements page. "Why not?" I thought. "Suits me better than treasure-seeking ever will."

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Hahaha. I would expect nothing less.
He nods and slips the notebook back into his pocket.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Good! I believe we have all we need from you.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Please, don't worry, Adèle. I see neither motive nor means for you to do her harm. You're all clear.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: But we'll get in touch if we need anything else. Oh, forgive me—another question. Was there anything else that seemed suspicious? Anything that stood out to you?

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: No, nothing really.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: Oh, wait!

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: There was a woman. I don't know if she's involved, but there was something odd about her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: It happened so fast, but still, while everyone else was too stunned to do anything, she sat there and smiled.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: She smiled? Do you recall what this woman looked like?
Adèle recounts the events as they happened. After hearing her out, the officer's professional demeanor cracks a little.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: Hah, that's Madame Beryl Bouanich. Couldn't be anyone else! Owns a crystal parlor on Rue de la Paix. She's a diviner, too.

items.speaker: Police Officer
items.text: She's the one who reported the case to us. Our officers have already spoken with her.

items.speaker: Adèle
items.text: She reported the case?
